external_narratives.summary: Walking guide and historical account of the Wellington Bomber R1465 crash site at Waun Rydd. The aircraft took off from the Operational Training Unit at Wellesbourne Mountford near Stratford-upon-Avon on 6 July 1942 for a cross-country training exercise.
external_narratives.key_details: Aircraft serial R1465. Pilot descended from the advised 10,000 ft in heavy cloud to try to fix position, striking the summit of Waun Rydd in a flat high-speed crash. All five crew were Canadian and are buried in Hereford.

external_narratives.summary: Article examining the Wellington crash site at Cwar y Gigfran (Raven's Quarry) on Waun Rydd, noting the extensive wreckage that remains visible at the site more than 80 years after the crash.
external_narratives.key_details: Two distinct piles of wreckage still remain at the site. The crash location is beneath Cwar y Gigfran ridge. A dedicated memorial cairn is often adorned with poppies by walkers.

narrative:
Wellington IC R1465 of 22 Operational Training Unit, based at Wellesbourne Mountford, flew into the summit of Waun Rydd in the Brecon Beacons on 6 July 1942. It was on a training flight. The aircraft carried practice bombs and reconnaissance flares and flew into low cloud. The pilot is believed to have come down from the advised 10,000 ft to check his position. All five crew died.

The five were Canadians serving in the RCAF. They were Flight Sergeant John Beverley Kemp, the pilot, aged 21, from Oakville, Ontario; Ernest Edward Mittell, aged 22, of Clinton, Ontario; Kenneth Ferguson Yuill, aged 30, of Winnipeg; Harold Creighton Beatty, a wireless operator; and James Patrick Hayes, an air gunner, whose parents lived in Souris, Manitoba. All five are buried at Hereford Cemetery.

The wreckage was spread over a large area and has since been gathered into two piles. The site is a Controlled Site under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986.
community_connection: A memorial cairn marks the site. The Coflein record says it was built by pupils and staff of Tredeger Comprehensive School. Walkers leave poppies, crosses and wreaths there.
